text:
sarah: Quick design check — I'm pulling together a small stopgap for the Playground streaming UI. Wanted feedback on a few things: placement of stop/regenerate, whether token counter should be live or debounce, and how the prompt-library quick-insert behaves during streaming. TL;DR: aim for minimal visual churn during live tokens.

mike: :eyes: love the goal. can you sketch where you want stop vs pause? also are we keeping both Stop and Regenerate as separate buttons in the composer, or a single affordance that morphs?

sarah: Thinking one persistent compact stop icon (square) on the message bubble, and a contextual regen button (↺) after completion. During streaming regen should be disabled. That avoids accidental regen mid-stream.

anika: Agree with disabling regen while streaming. For accessibility we should expose both as buttons in the toolbar for keyboard-only users — not only inline icons.

jordan: Token counter: live updates are noisy for some folks. Could we debounce to 300ms and only animate the counter when it changes >5 tokens? keeps things stable.

sarah: Good call. Debounce 300ms + threshold makes sense. Also propose compact mode where counter is collapsed to "●●" until hover/expand to reduce distraction.

liv-devex: Microcopy: change label from "Stop" to "Stop response" for clarity in screen readers. For regen use aria-label="Regenerate response". Also add aria-live politely on the streaming output container so screen readers announce final message only once.

anika: For prompt-library quick insert: if streaming is active, show a small toast: "Insert after current response completes" with an action "Queue insert". Otherwise immediate insert. Avoids mid-stream content injection.
mike: UX question: do we visually queue the prompt in the composer so user sees it pending? or keep it invisible to avoid confusion?
sarah: Let's queue it in a subtle inline chip in the composer: light border, small clock icon, "Queued: <prompt title>". Click to cancel. Keyboard accessible with esc to clear.
jordan: Edge case: user edits queued prompt before it's inserted — should we allow edit? My vote: allow edit, but if streaming completes and they hit send, we should confirm "Use edited queued prompt?" modal feels heavy. Maybe auto-apply edited version on insert and show undo snackbar.

liv-devex: A11y nit: ensure the queued chip is reachable via tab order and has role="status" so assistive tech sees queue changes. Also make sure color contrast meets AA.

aria-bot: Deploy snapshot: visual-spec v2.3.1 created for review by @sarah and @mike — link: https://figma.internal/redwood/playground/streaming/stopgap (preview expires in 7 days)

sarah: Thanks @aria-bot! Quick checklist before I update the mock: 1) debounce 300ms + >5 token animate threshold 2) stop icon inline + toolbar button 3) regen disabled during stream + aria-labels 4) queued prompt chip with cancel + editable content 5) queued toast when insert attempted mid-stream 6) ensure tab order + contrast. Anything missing?

anika: Add keyboard shortcut: Ctrl/Cmd+K to queue/insert prompt when focused in prompt library — document in help. Also include a11y docs snippet for screen reader behavior.
mike: Also confirm mobile: inline stop icon should be tappable and not conflict with selection gestures. maybe increase touch target to 44px.
sarah: Noted. I'll update prototype and push a small component PR. I'll flag in this thread when ready for quick pass. Thanks all :sparkles!
